newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Haider says his party is the PLO of Austria.
newsitem.headline: Haider says his party is the PLO of Austria.

text.p: Austrian far-right leader Joerg Haider, who landed huge gains in European parliamentary elections last week, described his Freedom Party as "the PLO of Austria" in a newspaper interview published on Friday.

Haider, never far from controversy, told Germany's Sueddeutsche Zeitung that the "authoritarian traits" of Austria's political system badly needed reforming and that only his party could liberate the Austrian people.
"We are the PLO of Austria, the Liberation movement of the Austrians," he said, accusing the establishment of displaying "pre-fascist" traits.

"These remarks are not only extremely damaging to Austria's reputation but represent a dangerous threat that provokes fear and terror," countered Brigitte Ederer, party manager of the ruling Social Democrats.

In Friday's interview Haider distanced himself from Austrian-born Adolf Hitler and insisted: "If I had lived in the time of National Socialism I would probably have been one of the people they locked up."
The populist leader was forced to resign as governor of Carinthia in 1991 after he praised Hitler's labour policies.

Haider claimed that beleaguered Chancellor Franz Vranitzky was his biggest aid in Sunday's poll, which brought his party a record 27.6 percent of the vote. The Socialist Democrats slumped to their lowest level since 1918.
"Without Vranitzky (there would have been) no advance for the Freedom Party," Haider said.
